     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# br-stub.sh: a stand-in for beads_rust (br) in the charting suites. No real beads database is
     3	# touched. State is a JSON array in $BR_STATE; every call is appended to $BR_LOG as one line of
     4	# space-joined argv. BR_FAIL_ON=<subcommand> makes that subcommand exit 1 (recovery tests).
     5	# Supported: --version, create, list, show, ready, update, dep add, comments add, close.
     6	set -euo pipefail
     7	: "${BR_STATE:?BR_STATE must be set}"
     8	: "${BR_LOG:=/dev/null}"
     9	[[ -f "$BR_STATE" ]] || echo '[]' > "$BR_STATE"
    10	printf '%s\n' "$*" >> "$BR_LOG"
    11	sub="${1:-}"; shift || true
    12	if [[ -n "${BR_FAIL_ON:-}" && "$sub" == "$BR_FAIL_ON" ]]; then echo "br-stub: forced failure of $sub" >&2; exit 1; fi
    13	save(){ local t; t="$(mktemp)"; cat > "$t"; mv "$t" "$BR_STATE"; }
    14	case "$sub" in
    15	  --version) echo "br 0.2.6-stub" ;;
    16	  create)
    17	    title=""; type="task"; parent=""; labels=""; ext=""; slug=""; desc=""; dry=0
    18	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    19	      case "$1" in
    20	        --type|-t) type="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    21	        --parent) parent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    22	        --labels|-l) labels="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    23	        --external-ref) ext="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    24	        --slug) slug="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    25	        --description|-d) desc="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    26	        --dry-run) dry=1; shift ;;
    27	        --json) shift ;;
    28	        -*) shift 2 ;;
    29	        *) title="$1"; shift ;;
    30	      esac
    31	    done
    32	    n="$(jq 'length' "$BR_STATE")"
    33	    id="bd-${slug:-x}-$((n + 1))"
    34	    obj="$(jq -cn --arg id "$id" --arg t "$title" --arg ty "$type" --arg p "$parent" --arg l "$labels" --arg e "$ext" --arg d "$desc" \
    35	      '{id:$id, title:$t, issue_type:$ty, status:"open", priority:2, assignee:null, description:$d,
    36	        labels:($l | split(",") | map(select(length > 0))), external_ref:(if $e == "" then null else $e end),
    37	        parent:(if $p == "" then null else $p end), deps:[], comments:[]}')"
    38	    if [[ $dry -eq 1 ]]; then printf '%s\n' "$obj" | jq -c '{dry_run: true, would_create: .}'; exit 0; fi
    39	    jq -c --argjson o "$obj" '. + [$o]' "$BR_STATE" | save
    40	    printf '%s\n' "$obj" ;;
    41	  list)
    42	    all=0; while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do case "$1" in --all|-a) all=1; shift ;; --json) shift ;; *) shift ;; esac; done
    43	    jq -c --argjson all "$all" '[.[] | select($all == 1 or .status != "closed")]' "$BR_STATE" ;;
    44	  show)
    45	    id="$1"; jq -ce --arg id "$id" '[.[] | select(.id == $id)] | if length == 0 then error("not found") else . end' "$BR_STATE" ;;
    46	  ready)
    47	    parent=""; types=()
    48	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do case "$1" in --parent) parent="$2"; shift 2 ;; --type|-t) types+=("$2"); shift 2 ;; --limit) shift 2 ;; *) shift ;; esac; done
    49	    ty="${types[0]:-}"
    50	    jq -c --arg p "$parent" --arg ty "$ty" '. as $all
    51	      | [.[] | select(.status == "open" and (.assignee == null))
    52	             | select($p == "" or .parent == $p) | select($ty == "" or .issue_type == $ty)
    53	             | select(all(.deps[]; . as $d | ($all | map(select(.id == $d)) | first | .status) == "closed"))]' "$BR_STATE" ;;
    54	  update)
    55	    id="$1"; shift
    56	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    57	      case "$1" in
    58	        --claim) jq -c --arg id "$id" 'map(if .id == $id then .status = "in_progress" | .assignee = "stub" else . end)' "$BR_STATE" | save; shift ;;
    59	        --add-label) jq -c --arg id "$id" --arg l "$2" 'map(if .id == $id then .labels += [$l] else . end)' "$BR_STATE" | save; shift 2 ;;
    60	        --status|-s) jq -c --arg id "$id" --arg s "$2" 'map(if .id == $id then .status = $s else . end)' "$BR_STATE" | save; shift 2 ;;
    61	        *) shift ;;
    62	      esac
    63	    done ;;
    64	  dep)
    65	    [[ "${1:-}" == "add" ]] || { echo "br-stub: dep $1 unsupported" >&2; exit 2; }
    66	    jq -c --arg a "$2" --arg b "$3" 'map(if .id == $a then .deps += [$b] else . end)' "$BR_STATE" | save ;;
    67	  comments)
    68	    [[ "${1:-}" == "add" ]] || { echo "br-stub: comments $1 unsupported" >&2; exit 2; }
    69	    jq -c --arg id "$2" --arg c "$3" 'map(if .id == $id then .comments += [$c] else . end)' "$BR_STATE" | save ;;
    70	  close)
    71	    id="$1"; shift; reason=""
    72	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do case "$1" in --reason|-r) reason="$2"; shift 2 ;; *) shift ;; esac; done
    73	    jq -e --arg id "$id" 'any(.[]; .id == $id)' "$BR_STATE" >/dev/null || { echo "br-stub: unknown $id" >&2; exit 1; }
    74	    jq -c --arg id "$id" --arg r "$reason" 'map(if .id == $id then .status = "closed" | .close_reason = $r else . end)' "$BR_STATE" | save ;;
    75	  *) echo "br-stub: unsupported subcommand '$sub'" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    76	esac

    22	| `decision:unblock` | a read-only probe settles a fact a decision waits on | `chart-unblock-probe.sh`, then the decision it unblocks |
    23

    25	probe that needs code runs in the throwaway worktree the probe helper creates and removes.

    29	Idea: "Move the hosted eval runner to self-hosted workers."

+# =============================================================================
+# Shared helpers for map and spike documents (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-3.17)
+# =============================================================================
+# Lines outside fenced code, prefixed "NR<TAB>" (inline code kept: a URL in
+# backticks is still a URL in the document).
+_md_unfenced_lines() {
+    LC_ALL=C awk '
+        /^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; next }
+        fence { next }
+        { printf "%d\t%s\n", NR, $0 }
+    ' "$FILE"
+}
+
+# D-3.17 plain prose: no URL in the document text, no blockquote run longer
+# than two lines (copied external text stays short). $1 names the repair.
+_md_prose_rules() {
+    local repair="$1" ln text
+    while IFS=$'\t' read -r ln text; do
+        [[ -n "$ln" ]] || continue
+        violations+=("$FILE:$ln: a URL in the document; ${repair}")
+    done < <(_md_unfenced_lines | grep -iE $'^[0-9]+\t.*https?://' || true)
+    local runs
+    runs="$(_md_unfenced_lines | LC_ALL=C awk -F'\t' '
+        $2 ~ /^[[:space:]]*>/ { if (!n) s = $1; n++; next }
+        { if (n > 2) printf "%d\t%d\n", s, n; n = 0 }
+        END { if (n > 2) printf "%d\t%d\n", s, n }
+    ')"
+    local start count
+    while IFS=$'\t' read -r start count; do
+        [[ -n "$start" ]] || continue
+        violations+=("$FILE:$start: a blockquote of $count lines; quote at most two lines of external text and cite the rest by path")
+    done <<< "$runs"
+}
+
+# pii-filter.sh over $FILE; $1 is the violation suffix.
+_md_pii_scan() {
+    local pii_filter="${SCRIPT_DIR}/pii-filter.sh"
+    if [[ -x "$pii_filter" ]]; then
+        local pii_result redactions
+        pii_result=$("$pii_filter" --file "$FILE" 2>/dev/null) || pii_result=""
+        if [[ -n "$pii_result" ]]; then
+            redactions=$(echo "$pii_result" | jq -r '.redactions // 0' 2>/dev/null) || redactions=0
+            if [[ "$redactions" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$redactions" -gt 0 ]]; then
+                violations+=("pii-filter.sh detected $redactions likely PII pattern(s) in $FILE; $1")
+            fi
+        fi
+    else
+        info_lines+=("pii-filter.sh not available; PII scan skipped")
+    fi
+}

+# The value of a '**Key**: value' header line (first match, trimmed).
+_md_header() {
+    grep -m1 -E "^\*\*$1\*\*:" -- "$FILE" | sed -E "s/^\*\*$1\*\*:[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]+\$//" || true
+}
+
+# The body of the H2 section named $1 (outside fenced code), blank lines dropped.
+_md_section_body() {
+    LC_ALL=C awk -v want="$1" '
+        /^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; if (sec) print; next }
+        !fence && /^## / { h = $0; sub(/^## +/, "", h); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", h); sec = (h == want); next }
+        !fence && /^# / { sec = 0; next }
+        sec && $0 ~ /[^[:space:]]/ { print }
+    ' "$FILE"
+}
+
+# H2 headings outside fenced code, "NR<TAB>title".
+_md_h2_list() {
+    LC_ALL=C awk '
+        /^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; next }
+        !fence && /^## / { h = $0; sub(/^## +/, "", h); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", h); printf "%d\t%s\n", NR, h }
+    ' "$FILE"
+}

+# Beads cross-checks run against the project's own tracker only: br on PATH,
+# a .beads/ directory at the project root, and the validated file inside the
+# project (a fixture elsewhere has no relation to this project's beads).
+_beads_crosscheck_available() {
+    command -v br >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
+    [[ -d "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.beads" ]] || return 1
+    local root dir
+    root="$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" || return 1
+    dir="$(cd "$(dirname -- "$FILE")" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" || return 1
+    [[ "$dir/" == "$root/"* ]]

+# br <args> run at the project root, stdout only; normalised to a JSON array
+# of issues ("list" replies are {issues: [...]}, "show" replies are arrays).
+_br_json_array() {
+    local out
+    out="$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && br "$@" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
+    printf '%s' "$out" | jq -c 'if type == "array" then . elif type == "object" then (.issues // [.]) else [] end' 2>/dev/null

+# =============================================================================
+# sprint: no question bead carries a sprint: label or sits under a sprint epic
+# (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-4.7 d, A16)
+# =============================================================================
+validate_sprint_beads() {
+    if ! _beads_crosscheck_available; then
+        info_lines+=("beads cross-check skipped (needs br, ${PROJECT_ROOT}/.beads and the plan inside the project): question beads were not checked for sprint labels")
+        return 0
+    fi
+    local questions epics
+    if ! questions="$(_br_json_array list --type question --limit 0 --json)" \
+       || ! epics="$(_br_json_array list --type epic --all --limit 0 --json)"; then
+        warnings+=("br list failed; the question-bead sprint cross-check did not run")
+        return 0
+    fi
+    local hits
+    hits="$(jq -rn --argjson q "$questions" --argjson e "$epics" '
+        def labels: [(.labels // [])[] | if type == "object" then (.name // "") else tostring end];
+        ($e | map(select(labels | any(startswith("sprint:")))) | map(.id)) as $sprint_epics
+        | $q[]
+        | . as $b
+        | (labels) as $l
+        | ([$l[] | select(startswith("sprint:"))]) as $sl
+        | ([(.dependencies // [])[] | select((.type // .dependency_type // "") == "parent-child") | (.depends_on_id // .id // "")]
+           + [$l[] | select(startswith("epic:")) | ltrimstr("epic:")]) as $parents

+    while IFS=$'\t' read -r kind id what; do

+# map: a /chart decision map document (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-4.8, §4.2)
+# =============================================================================
+MAP_SECTIONS=("Destination" "Decisions so far" "Not yet specified" "Out of scope")
+MAP_STATUSES="charting handed-off closed abandoned"
+BEAD_ID_RE='^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$'

+validate_map() {
+    local slug status epic
+    slug="$(_md_header Slug)"; status="$(_md_header Status)"; epic="$(_md_header Epic)"
+    if [[ -z "$slug" ]]; then
+        violations+=("no '**Slug**:' header line; add '**Slug**: <slug>' under the title (see grimoires/loa/sdd.md §4.2)")
+    elif ! [[ "$slug" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$ ]]; then
+        violations+=("**Slug** '$slug' is not a slug (letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'; 64 characters at most)")
+    fi
+    if [[ -z "$status" ]]; then
+        violations+=("no '**Status**:' header line; add '**Status**: charting' (one of: $MAP_STATUSES)")
+    elif [[ " $MAP_STATUSES " != *" $status "* ]]; then
+        violations+=("**Status** '$status' is not one of: $MAP_STATUSES")
+    fi
+    if [[ -z "$epic" ]]; then
+        violations+=("no '**Epic**:' header line; add '**Epic**: <bead-id>' naming the map epic")
+    elif ! [[ "$epic" =~ $BEAD_ID_RE ]]; then
+        violations+=("**Epic** '$epic' is not a bead id")
+    fi
+
+    local h1s
+    h1s="$(_md_unfenced_lines | grep -cE $'^[0-9]+\t# ' || true)"
+    if [[ "${h1s:-0}" -ne 1 ]]; then
+        violations+=("a map doc has exactly one H1 ('# Map: <title>'); found ${h1s:-0}")
+    fi
+
+    # H2 allowlist, in order, plus an optional final '## Closed'. Any other H2
+    # is refused: a map plans and never carries execution instructions.
+    local ln title idx=0 seen_closed=false
+    while IFS=$'\t' read -r ln title; do
+        [[ -n "$ln" ]] || continue
+        if [[ "$seen_closed" == true ]]; then
+            violations+=("$FILE:$ln: '## $title' after '## Closed'; '## Closed' is the last section of a map doc")
+            continue
+        fi
+        if [[ "$title" == "Closed" ]]; then
+            seen_closed=true
+            continue
+        fi
+        if [[ $idx -lt ${#MAP_SECTIONS[@]} && "$title" == "${MAP_SECTIONS[$idx]}" ]]; then
+            idx=$((idx + 1))
+            continue
+        fi
+        local known=false s
+        for s in "${MAP_SECTIONS[@]}"; do [[ "$title" == "$s" ]] && known=true; done
+        if [[ "$known" == true ]]; then
+            violations+=("$FILE:$ln: '## $title' is out of order or repeated; the sections are, in order: ${MAP_SECTIONS[*]/#/## }")
+        else
+            violations+=("$FILE:$ln: '## $title' is not a map section; a map doc has exactly Destination, Decisions so far, Not yet specified and Out of scope (then an optional Closed), and carries no execution instructions")
+        fi
+    done < <(_md_h2_list)
+    if [[ $idx -lt ${#MAP_SECTIONS[@]} ]]; then
+        local i
+        for (( i = idx; i < ${#MAP_SECTIONS[@]}; i++ )); do
+            grep -qxF "## ${MAP_SECTIONS[$i]}" -- "$FILE" || violations+=("missing section '## ${MAP_SECTIONS[$i]}' (see grimoires/loa/sdd.md §4.2)")
+        done
+    fi
+    [[ -n "$(_md_section_body "Destination")" ]] || violations+=("'## Destination' is empty; state what is true when the effort is done (three sentences at most)")
+
+    local bullet
+    while IFS= read -r bullet; do
+        [[ -n "$bullet" ]] || continue
+        [[ "$bullet" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[-*][[:space:]] ]] || continue
+        [[ "$bullet" =~ DEC-[0-9]{4,} ]] || violations+=("a 'Decisions so far' bullet cites no DEC row: '${bullet:0:120}'; the form is '- <name> (DEC-NNNN, <bead-id>): <one line>'")
+    done < <(_md_section_body "Decisions so far")
+
+    _md_prose_rules "cite a repo path or a grimoires/loa/research/ report instead"
+    _md_pii_scan "a map doc is tracked state, remove them"
+
+    [[ -n "$epic" && "$epic" =~ $BEAD_ID_RE ]] || return 0
+    if ! _beads_crosscheck_available; then
+        warnings+=("beads cross-check skipped (needs br, ${PROJECT_ROOT}/.beads and the map inside the project): the children of $epic were not checked")
+        return 0
+    fi
+    _validate_map_beads "$epic" "$status" "$slug"
+}

+ice_gh_stub() {

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# charting-decisions.bats: the /chart command, the charting-decisions skill frontmatter, the map
     3	# template and the shell steps the skill calls (chart-guard.sh, chart-ticket.sh,
     4	# chart-unblock-probe.sh). SDD D-4.1 to D-4.5, D-4.10 to D-4.12.
     5	#
     6	# Hermetic: .claude/scripts is copied into a fresh git repo per file, so the decision-ledger
     7	# writer sees no live run state, no autonomous PRD and no main checkout. beads is a PATH stub
     8	# (tests/fixtures/charting/br-stub.sh); the ledger is a --ledger fixture outside the tree.
     9	
    10	setup_file() {
    11	    export REAL_ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    12	    export H="$BATS_FILE_TMPDIR/proj"
    13	    mkdir -p "$H/.claude"
    14	    cp -R "$REAL_ROOT/.claude/scripts" "$H/.claude/scripts"
    15	    git -C "$H" init -q
    16	    git -C "$H" -c user.email=t@example.invalid -c user.name=t commit -q --allow-empty -m init
    17	    mkdir -p "$BATS_FILE_TMPDIR/bin"
    18	    cp "$REAL_ROOT/tests/fixtures/charting/br-stub.sh" "$BATS_FILE_TMPDIR/bin/br"
    19	    chmod +x "$BATS_FILE_TMPDIR/bin/br"
    20	}
    21	
    22	setup() {
    23	    unset LOA_UNATTENDED LOA_FLATLINE_MODE CI GITHUB_ACTIONS LOA_HOOK_CONTEXT BR_FAIL_ON
    24	    rm -rf "$H/grimoires" "$H/.run" "$H/.beads"
    25	    mkdir -p "$H/grimoires/loa/maps" "$H/grimoires/loa/research" "$H/grimoires/loa/context" "$H/.beads"
    26	    export BR_STATE="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/br-state.json" BR_LOG="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/br.log"
    27	    echo '[]' > "$BR_STATE"; : > "$BR_LOG"
    28	    export LEDGER="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/decisions.yaml"
    29	    printf 'schema_version: 1\ndecisions: []\n' > "$LEDGER"
    30	    export PATH="$BATS_FILE_TMPDIR/bin:$PATH"
    31	    CT="$H/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh"
    32	    GUARD="$H/.claude/scripts/chart-guard.sh"
    33	    SKILL="$REAL_ROOT/.claude/skills/charting-decisions/SKILL.md"
    34	    TEMPLATE="$REAL_ROOT/.claude/skills/charting-decisions/resources/templates/map.md"
    35	}
    36

    41	    [[ "$block" == *"halt: create the same bead and row, then stop planning"* ]]

#
# Exit codes:
#   Command's exit code on normal completion
#   124 on timeout (matches GNU timeout convention)
#
# Usage:
#   run_with_timeout 30 grep -rn "pattern" ./src
#   run_with_timeout 5 git ls-remote "$url" HEAD
#
run_with_timeout() {
  local timeout_val="$1"
  shift

  # Runtime detection (not cached) to support test PATH manipulation
  if command -v timeout &>/dev/null; then
    timeout "$timeout_val" "$@"
  elif command -v gtimeout &>/dev/null; then
    gtimeout "$timeout_val" "$@"
  elif command -v perl &>/dev/null; then
    # fork+exec pattern preserves $SIG{ALRM} handler in the parent.
    # bare exec would replace the process image, losing the handler.
    # IMPORTANT: Extract timeout and fork BEFORE setting alarm —
    # if alarm fires before fork returns, $pid is undef and
    # kill(9, undef) sends SIGKILL to process group 0.
    perl -e '
      my $timeout = shift @ARGV;
      my $pid = fork();
      die "fork failed: $!" unless defined $pid;
      if ($pid == 0) { exec @ARGV; die "exec failed: $!" }
      $SIG{ALRM} = sub { kill 9, $pid; exit 124 };
      alarm($timeout);
      waitpid($pid, 0);
      alarm(0);
      exit($? >> 8);
    ' "$timeout_val" "$@"
  else
    echo "WARNING: No timeout mechanism available, running without timeout" >&2
    "$@"
  fi
}

  fi
  return 0
}
# Two scopes. A live signal (fresh marker, RUNNING run state, LOA_UNATTENDED=1, autonomous Flatline mode)
# means no operator is at the keyboard: it governs attribution, the operator-only operations and the
# `context` verdict. The PRD Status line is a planning-time default only: it makes `new` and `decide`

}

}

lock_path(){ # target -> lock file under .run, keyed by the target's absolute path
  local abs h
  abs="$(abs_dir "$(dirname "$1")")/$(basename "$1")"
  h="$(printf '%s' "$abs" | sha256_portable | cut -c1-12)"
  printf '%s' "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.run/.dec-write-${h}.lock"
}
acquire_lock(){ # target
  local lp; lp="$(lock_path "$1")"
  mkdir -p "${PROJECT_ROOT}/.run"
  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ "${LOA_DEC_NO_FLOCK:-0}" != "1" ]]; then
    exec 9>"$lp"
    flock -w "$LOCK_WAIT" 9 || die "lock busy: another writer holds ${lp} (waited ${LOCK_WAIT}s); retry"
    return 0
  fi
  local d="${lp}.d" tries=$(( LOCK_WAIT * 10 )) pid
  while ! mkdir "$d" 2>/dev/null; do
    pid="$(cat "$d/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    # Stale: older than 60 s and its owner is gone.
    if [[ -n "$(find "$d" -maxdepth 0 -mmin +1 2>/dev/null)" ]] && { [[ -z "$pid" ]] || ! kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; }; then

    fi
    tries=$(( tries - 1 ))

    sleep 0.1
  done
  MKLOCK="$d"
  printf '%s\n' "$$" > "$d/pid"
}

> # FR-6 heredoc consumer classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1; knob

> #   _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   → prints interpreter|nonexec|none

> # Bash 3.2 compatible (no ${x,,}, no mapfile, no associative arrays) and safe
> # under a caller's `set -u`.
> #
> # Grammar (literal command text; no alias or function expansion; CRLF folded
> # to LF). The command is walked line by line; a line holding an unquoted
> # `<<` / `<<-` (not `<<<`) is a heredoc header, the body runs to the first
> # line equal to the delimiter (leading tabs stripped for `<<-`). FULL SCAN

> # tokenizer cannot read (open quote, trailing backslash, comment), more than

> # \W or W with W in [A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]; `$X` is a variable delimiter), or a

> #   interpreter — body scanned exactly as today: the header holds `$(`, a

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# FR-SZ2 — System-Zone (.claude/) direct Bash writes (cycle-122)
# Closes the single-agent gap: zone-write-guard fences Write/Edit tools, the
# team guards fence teammates, but a plain-shell `echo x > .claude/foo` or
# `sed -i` on a hook passed every wired fence. Same trust posture as
# zone-write-guard: the bounded framework-dev marker
# (.run/zone-guard-authorization.json — scope=framework, RFC3339 expires_at,
# 24h mtime cap; test override via LOA_ZONE_GUARD_AUTH_FILE) authorizes
# upstream self-development sessions, audited per-session. Sanctioned paths
# `.claude/overrides/` and `.claude/cache/` are excluded (they are the
# documented customization/runtime surfaces). LOA_ALLOW_STATE_ZONE_EXEC_WRITE=1
# is honored with the same warn+audit semantics as FR-SZ.
# Shapes: redirect, tee, copy-family dest, sed-in-place, rm. Same accepted
# bypass classes as FR-SZ (fence, not boundary).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [[ "$_cmd_match" == *".."* ]]; then
  # traversal-looking command: no exclusions (a path like
  # .claude/overrides/../hooks/x resolves back into protected space)
  _c2_cmd="$_cmd_match"
else
  _c2_cmd="${_cmd_match//.claude\/overrides/.EXCLUDED-OVR}"
  _c2_cmd="${_c2_cmd//.claude\/cache/.EXCLUDED-CACHE}"
fi
if [[ "$_c2_cmd" == *".claude/"* ]]; then
  _c2_file="\\.claude/${_sz_pc}+"
  _c2_tgt="\\.claude(/${_sz_pc}*)?"
  _c2_authorized=""
  # 1) env override (operator terminals) — same var as FR-SZ
  if [[ "${LOA_ALLOW_STATE_ZONE_EXEC_WRITE:-}" == "1" ]]; then
    _c2_authorized="env"
  else
    # 2) bounded framework-dev marker (mirrors zone-write-guard validation)
    _c2_auth_file="${LOA_ZONE_GUARD_AUTH_FILE:-${LOA_REPO_ROOT:-.}/.run/zone-guard-authorization.json}"
    if [[ -f "$_c2_auth_file" ]] && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      _c2_row="$(jq -r 'select(type=="object" and .scope=="framework"
                          and (.reason|type=="string") and ((.reason|length)>0)
                          and (.expires_at|type=="string")
                          and (.expires_at|test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z$")))
                        | .expires_at' "$_c2_auth_file" 2>/dev/null)" || _c2_row=""
      if [[ -n "$_c2_row" ]]; then
        TZ=UTC0 printf -v _c2_now '%(%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)T' -1
        printf -v _c2_epoch '%(%s)T' -1
        _c2_mtime="$(stat -Lc '%Y' -- "$_c2_auth_file" 2>/dev/null || stat -Lf '%m' -- "$_c2_auth_file" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
        if [[ "$_c2_mtime" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( _c2_epoch - _c2_mtime <= 86400 )) && [[ "$_c2_now" < "$_c2_row" ]]; then
          _c2_authorized="marker"
        fi
      fi
    fi

# Reviewer concerns — sprint-1 (PR: /chart decision map + prototype-ticket discipline)

Scope: pr/head.diff (41 files). Cite head/<path>:<line>.

Concerns found so far (verify, extend, dissent):

1. chart-unblock-probe.sh runs arbitrary argv in a worktree that SHARES the main .git directory,
   with the session's full environment (credentials, SSH agent). It only compares
   `git status --porcelain` of the main tree before/after. Ref rewrites (`git branch -f`,
   `git update-ref`), hook installs under .git/hooks, config edits, and `git push` are invisible
   to that check and exit 0.
2. git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored=matching does not list new files under a
   directory ignored by a `dir/` pattern (repo .gitignore has `grimoires/loa/context/`). The
   research-end scope check (chart-ticket.sh) and the probe therefore miss writes to
   grimoires/loa/context/*.md, which /plan-and-analyze auto-loads as priority context. The
   chart-researcher agent has the Write tool and processes WebFetch content.
3. chart-ticket.sh close --consumed-by has no status/open-row precondition and no context check;
   chart-guard --close-consumed passes unattended. An unattended run can close a `charting` map
   and reject every open decision row.
4. Interactive-only rule is enforced only by prose (Step 0 chart-guard) — chart-ticket.sh write
   subcommands (epic/ticket/resolve/rule-out/handoff/research-*) carry no context check.
5. chart.md command context_files auto-loads grimoires/loa/research/chart-*.md (untrusted
   research reports) unfenced into the session context; plan-and-analyze.md context_files glob
   loads every chart-*.md snapshot, contradicting the "other snapshots are not ingested" rule.
6. section_append / set_status pass operator text through `awk -v`, which interprets backslash
   escapes (`\n`) — a --line/--why value can inject new lines/headings into the map doc.
7. handoff inlines the map doc and ledger rows unfenced (only research reports pass the L6
   sanitizer); heading demotion `sed` also rewrites lines inside fenced code.
8. get-ready-work.sh filters on `.issue_type` only; chart-frontier/chart-ticket accept `.type` too.
   create-sprint-task.sh treats a reply without `labels` or an {issues:[...]} envelope as "not a map".
9. resolve: --answer-ref optional; dec-write-lib drops it unattended, so rows without operator
   reference can be handed off as "settled".
10. SP-1 misses: `git reset --hard spike/x`, `git checkout -B feature spike/x`, `git switch -c`,
    `git read-tree`, `git archive`; FR-1.1 spike-delete predicate.
11. run-mode-ice safe_merge: `git merge --no-edit` without --ff may fail under merge.ff=only;
    is_spike_branch matches any `*/spike/*`.
12. Docs: no CHANGELOG entry, no CLAUDE.loa.md entry for the new /chart command; tests reference
    grimoires/loa/spikes/TEMPLATE.md which this PR does not add.
13. Tests: CD-10 (autonomous PRD) and CD-27 (probe) failed in my run — verify root cause.

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-20
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (pr/PR.md)

---

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is `pr/head.diff`: the `/chart` decision-map workflow (command, skill, researcher agent, four shell helpers, map/spike validators), the prototype-ticket discipline (spike branches in the safety hook and ICE, `interview.unattended_prototype`), and the build-path lints that keep `question` beads out of sprints. The design intent is sound and well documented, the write-order/idempotency rules in `chart-ticket.sh` hold in the fixture suites, and the fence-corpus rows for SP-1 all replay correctly against the head hook.

The defects are concentrated where the PR promises a mechanical boundary and delivers a check that can be walked around: the unblock probe only diffs `git status` text while sharing the main `.git` and the session environment; the research scope check cannot see writes under an ignored directory that the planner later auto-loads; `close --consumed-by` and every other `chart-ticket.sh` write run unattended with no context check; the spike-delete predicate fails open on an unparsable ledger (the PR's own test for that case fails); and `awk -v` turns a `\n` in a decision line into a new section of the map doc. Each is reproduced below on the head scripts (run from a fixture tree built from `pr/head`).

Process notes: `reviewer.md` carries only the PR title, so there is no `## AC Verification` walkthrough (an automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED trigger under this skill on its own). Fast gate: no formatter or type checker applies to this shell/markdown change; `bats` was run on the PR's suites. Of the 29 charting-decisions cases 28 pass (CD-10 fails, see Observations); chart-frontier, charting-lint and golden-path-charting pass in full (48/48); spike-validator fails 3 of 16 (two need the absent `grimoires/loa/spikes/TEMPLATE.md`, one is the fail-open predicate below); the 9 map-validator cases, unattended-prototype and the ICE spike cases pass.

Grounding: "Any difference fails the probe" is not what the shipped helper does — it "exits 1 when the main tree's status changed" (`head/.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh:11`); "a map can never carry an execution override" (`head/.claude/skills/charting-decisions/SKILL.md:164`); "/chart is interactive only" (`head/.claude/scripts/chart-guard.sh:5`).

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Security — the unblock probe is not a sandbox

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh:66` — the probe argv runs with the session's full environment (credentials, SSH agent socket, HOME, git config) inside a detached worktree that shares the main repository's `.git` directory; a probe command lifted from a ticket body or a research report can push, fetch or write with the operator's identity.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh:66`
**Issue:** `(cd "$WT" && run_with_timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$@")` scrubs nothing. Reproduced: `SECRET_TOKEN=abc chart-unblock-probe.sh --ticket bd-x -- bash -c 'echo $SECRET_TOKEN $HOME'` prints the token and the real home.
**Why This Matters:** `decision:unblock` is sold as "the only way an unblock ticket runs anything" (line 3) and the skill allows `Bash(.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh *)`; the operator is told a probe "never writes App-Zone code in the main tree", not that it inherits every credential of the session.
**Required Fix:** run the argv under `env -i` with PATH, a scratch HOME/TMPDIR, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, an empty `credential.helper`, a failing `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`/askpass; have the skill show the operator the exact argv and confirm before running.
**Reference:** CWE-250 (execution with unnecessary privileges), CWE-526 (cleartext sensitive information in an environment variable).

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh:71-75` — the post-run verdict compares `git status --porcelain` text only; ref rewrites, hook installs, `git config` edits and overwrites of an already-modified tracked file leave the status identical, so the helper prints `probe-exit: 0` and exits 0.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh:71`
**Issue:** Reproduced on the head script: (1) `bash -c 'echo x > f && git add f && git commit -qm evil && git branch -f keep HEAD'` moved branch `keep` to a probe-authored commit, exit 0; (2) writing `.git/hooks/post-checkout` from the worktree, exit 0 and the hook is present in the main repo; (3) `git config core.hooksPath /evil`, exit 0 and the main repo's config now points at `/evil`. The dissent adds the same-status case: a tracked file already ` M` can be rewritten through its absolute path without changing a porcelain line (DISS-001).
**Why This Matters:** the worktree shares refs, hooks and config with the main checkout; the main tree the operator commits from next is already compromised while the ticket records "main tree unchanged".
**Required Fix:** snapshot `git for-each-ref`, HEAD, a hash of `config`/`config.worktree`, a listing plus hashes of `hooks/`, and the porcelain status before and after; add a marker file and fail on any file under the main tree or the common git dir (excluding `objects/`, `worktrees/`) newer than it; create the worktree with `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null`.
**Reference:** CWE-284 (improper access control); OWASP ASVS V14 configuration integrity.

### 2. Decision-ledger integrity — unattended paths

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:402-404` — `close --consumed-by` has no precondition on the map's `**Status**` or on open rows and no context check, and `chart-guard.sh:45-48` passes `--close-consumed` in an unattended context; an unattended `/plan-and-analyze` (or any agent naming the wrong slug) closes a map that is still `charting` and rejects every undecided row.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:402`
**Issue:** Reproduced: a `charting` map with three open rows, `LOA_UNATTENDED=1 chart-ticket.sh close --map m1 --consumed-by cycle-9` → exit 0, `**Status**: closed`, ledger rows `["rejected","rejected","rejected"]`, tickets and epic closed. `chart-guard.sh --close-consumed` printed `unattended` and exit 0 for the same tree. The dissent reaches the same conclusion from both voices (DISS-003, DISS-C-001).
**Why This Matters:** the one unattended exception exists to retire a *consumed* map; here it retires the operator's open decisions with `agent` attribution, irreversibly for the rows (rejected rows are not re-opened).
**Required Fix:** in `op_close`, when `--consumed-by` is given require `doc_field Status == handed-off` and zero open rows, else `die` and write nothing; make a repeated close of an already `closed|abandoned` map a no-op so the planner's re-run is safe.

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:159-240, 242-260, 291-349, 351-396, 438-471` — none of `epic`, `ticket`, `edge`, `claim`, `resolve`, `rule-out`, `handoff`, `research-begin`, `research-end` checks the interactive context; only `close --reason` does (`:407-408`). The interactive-only rule therefore lives in skill prose (`head/.claude/skills/charting-decisions/SKILL.md:69-74`, "run chart-guard.sh first, every time"), which an unattended command, `/run`, or a skill that skips Step 0 does not execute.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:159`
**Issue:** Reproduced with `LOA_UNATTENDED=1`: `epic` exit 0, `ticket` exit 0 (row + bead written), `resolve` exit 0 (row moved to `proposed`, bead closed, doc line added). `--answer-ref` is optional (`:304`) and `handoff` (`:351-360`) never checks that resolved rows carry an operator reference, so a map "whose rounds the agent answered" (SDD D-4.3: "is not a map") is handed off under the heading "these decisions are settled; confirm, do not re-ask".
**Why This Matters:** the PR's own design statement (`chart-guard.sh:5-9`) and the project's "mechanical stack" principle both require the refusal to be enforced by the helper, not by the prose that invokes it. Confidence is medium only because an attended `/chart` session that follows Step 0 never hits the gap.
**Required Fix:** add a `need_interactive` precondition (same `dec-write-lib.sh context --prd …` call as `chart-guard.sh`, fail closed on anything but `interactive`, `--dry-run` exempt) to every write subcommand; make `--answer-ref` required on `resolve`; in `handoff`, refuse when any `proposed|decided` row of the map lacks `decided_by_ref`.

### 3. Research scope check — writes the check cannot see

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:457-458` — `research-end` diffs `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored=matching` snapshots. Git never lists new files inside a directory ignored by a `dir/` pattern (the directory shows as one `!!` line before and after), and `head/.gitignore:312` ignores `grimoires/loa/context/` that way. A researcher write to `grimoires/loa/context/chart-injected.md` passed `research-end` (reproduced: exit 0, report path printed) and that directory is exactly what `head/.claude/commands/plan-and-analyze.md:44` and `:50` auto-load as priority-1 and priority-2 context.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:458`
**Issue:** the `chart-researcher` agent keeps the Write tool (`head/.claude/agents/chart-researcher.md:5`) and processes WebFetch pages; its one-file rule (`:24`) is prose. The mechanical check that is supposed to catch a stray write only handles `.run/` and `.beads/` specially (`:459-462`) and is blind to every other ignored directory (`grimoires/loa/context/`, `grimoires/loa/visions/`, `grimoires/loa/memory/`, …). Two voices of the dissent flag the same path (DISS-C-003).
**Why This Matters:** a prompt-injected web page becomes a fabricated hand-off snapshot or context file that the next `/plan-and-analyze` reads as "settled decisions; do not re-ask" — the untrusted-data boundary the PR says it fences (SKILL.md:160-161).
**Required Fix:** remove `Write` from the researcher's tools and have the session write the returned report itself (then the check is secondary), or at minimum add an mtime sweep over the whole project tree (`find … -newer marker`, excluding the report path) and exempt only this map's own report paths rather than all of `grimoires/loa/research/`.
**Reference:** CWE-20 (improper input validation), OWASP LLM01 (prompt injection), LLM08 (excessive agency).

### 4. Safety hook — the spike-delete predicate fails open

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:651-657` — `yq -o=json -I0 '.'
